value.rationale: The varying even-power adjacent equality is a natural exact Diophantine problem. An explicit O(d) total candidate count around three 3-adically selected exponentially large centers is a strong, effective structural reduction from an unbounded search and separates possible future examples by residue class. The precision is essential: a basic crude height bound would leave exponentially many candidates. This is mathematically useful even absent an existence theorem.
